parent_baseline: ../model_parameters.json (build f22971e, frictionless recoupled baseline -- this file is a standalone copy, not a diff/import, so the sub-branch has no path dependency on the parent)

parameter_notes._carried_over: L, N_r, T_hold, T_d, I_m, I_c, I_s, I_sb, M_screw, M_s, k_c, k_s1, k_s2, k_brg, c_c, c_s1, c_s2, c_brg, c_EM are unchanged copies from the frictionless baseline (Rev 4/model_parameters.json). See that file's parameter_notes for their provenance.
parameter_notes._dropped: k_nut and c_nut from the baseline are REMOVED here, not carried over. In the baseline they embedded the screw-nut interface as a rigid (non-slipping) linear spring/damper directly in K/C. That was always flagged as a tradeoff (backlog.md issue set, Sec. 10 item 3 of state_space_6dof.md): it assumes the nut never slips. This sub-branch replaces that assumption with an explicit LuGre friction port at the nut interface (sigma0_nut etc.), so keeping k_nut/c_nut in K/C as well would double-count the same physical compliance (the exact 'interface double path' problem flagged as Sec. 10 item 2 in the original, pre-recoupled derivation).
parameter_notes.sigma0_nut: Nut presliding (bristle) stiffness, N/m. PLACEHOLDER. Reused from Rev 3 'n_sigma0' (GMS nut-site stiffness sum) -- Rev 3's GMS model and this LuGre model are different friction formalisms, but n_sigma0 is the closest available presliding-stiffness estimate for this exact interface. Notably softer than k_nut=1e8 N/m from the baseline: friction presliding compliance is a separate, much softer mechanism riding underneath the stiffer Hertzian ball-groove contact stiffness that k_nut represented.
parameter_notes.sigma1_nut: Nut micro-damping, N*s/m. PLACEHOLDER. Reused from Rev 3 'n_sigma1' = 0.0 (Rev 3 did not identify this term separately from sigma0/sigma2 either).
parameter_notes.sigma2_nut: Nut viscous coefficient, N*s/m. PLACEHOLDER. Reused from Rev 3 'n_sigma2'.
parameter_notes.Fc_nut: Nut Coulomb (kinetic) friction force, N. PLACEHOLDER, not given anywhere in the workspace. Derived from Rev 3 'F_preload_nut'=100N and 'eta_screw'=0.9: lead angle lambda=atan(L/(pi*screw_diameter))=atan(1e-3/(pi*8e-3))=2.28deg (screw_diameter from Rev 3); solving eta=tan(lambda)/tan(lambda+phi) for the friction angle phi gives phi=0.25deg, i.e. mu=tan(phi)=0.0044 (very low, consistent with a ball screw, not a sliding Acme screw). Fc_nut = mu*F_preload_nut = 0.0044*100 = 0.5 N (rounded).
parameter_notes.Fs_nut: Nut static (stiction) friction force, N. PLACEHOLDER. Fs=1.5*Fc, a generic static/kinetic ratio placeholder (no measured Stribeck ratio available for this interface).
parameter_notes.vs_nut: Nut Stribeck velocity, m/s. PLACEHOLDER. Reused from Rev 3 'n_vs'.
parameter_notes.sigma0_sb: Support bearing presliding stiffness, N*m/rad. PLACEHOLDER. Originally reused directly from Rev 3 'd_sigma0'=3.0e6 (by elimination: Rev 3's three GMS parameter sets are prefixed d_/g_/n_, and n_/g_ map unambiguously to nut/guideway by name, leaving d_ for the support bearing) -- but that value paired with I_sb=1.5e-7 kg*m^2 gives a bristle natural frequency sqrt(sigma0/I_sb) of ~712 kHz, absurdly stiff versus every structural mode in this system (max ~6863 Hz) and severe enough that it made both Radau and BDF diverge to NaN during solver testing (2026-08-18) regardless of tolerance/max_step settings -- confirming the cross-domain-reuse caveat originally written here. Revised down to 500 N*m/rad, which puts the bristle mode at ~9.2 kHz: comparable to k_s1/k_s2=211 N*m/rad (a similar order of magnitude to the screw's own torsional stiffness) and just above the system's highest existing linear mode, instead of three orders of magnitude beyond it. Still an unmeasured placeholder, just no longer numerically pathological.
parameter_notes.sigma1_sb: Support bearing micro-damping, N*m*s/rad. PLACEHOLDER. Reused from Rev 3 'd_sigma1' = 0.0.
parameter_notes.sigma2_sb: Support bearing viscous coefficient, N*m*s/rad. PLACEHOLDER. Reused from Rev 3 'd_sigma2'.
parameter_notes.Tc_sb: Support bearing Coulomb friction torque, N*m. PLACEHOLDER, not given anywhere in the workspace. Rolling-element bearing running torque is typically a small fraction of the motor's own torque scale; set to ~2.5% of 'holding_torque'=0.06 N*m as an order-of-magnitude guess.
parameter_notes.Ts_sb: Support bearing static friction torque, N*m. PLACEHOLDER. Ts=1.47*Tc, matching the Fs/Fc ratio used for the nut interface.
parameter_notes.vs_sb: Support bearing Stribeck velocity, rad/s. PLACEHOLDER. Reused from Rev 3 'd_vs' (same cross-domain caveat as sigma0_sb).
parameter_notes.sigma0_way: Guideway presliding stiffness, N/m. PLACEHOLDER. Reused from Rev 3 'g_sigma0'.
parameter_notes.sigma1_way: Guideway micro-damping, N*s/m. PLACEHOLDER. Reused from Rev 3 'g_sigma1' = 0.0.
parameter_notes.sigma2_way: Guideway viscous coefficient, N*s/m. PLACEHOLDER. Reused from Rev 3 'g_sigma2'.
parameter_notes.Fc_way: Guideway Coulomb friction force, N. PLACEHOLDER, not given anywhere in the workspace. Linear guide rails (preloaded, with wipers/seals) typically run higher friction than a lubricated ball nut; set a few times Fc_nut as an order-of-magnitude guess.
parameter_notes.Fs_way: Guideway static friction force, N. PLACEHOLDER. Fs=1.5*Fc, same ratio placeholder as the other two interfaces.
parameter_notes.vs_way: Guideway Stribeck velocity, m/s. PLACEHOLDER. Reused from Rev 3 'g_vs'.
